nodes.label: IRB Application Pack Requirement & Overview: Banks intending to adopt the Internal Ratings-Based approach must submit a completed IRB application pack signed by the CEO and board chairperson.
nodes.norm_label: irb application pack requirement & overview: banks intending to adopt the internal ratings-based approach must submit a completed irb application pack signed by the ceo and board chairperson.

nodes.label: 18-Month Application Period: Banks should allow up to 18 months between submitting the IRB application pack and receiving approval or denial.
nodes.norm_label: 18-month application period: banks should allow up to 18 months between submitting the irb application pack and receiving approval or denial.

nodes.label: Parallel Reporting Run Requirement: All IRB applicant banks must undertake a minimum six-month parallel reporting run for affected portfolios during the 18-month application period.
nodes.norm_label: parallel reporting run requirement: all irb applicant banks must undertake a minimum six-month parallel reporting run for affected portfolios during the 18-month application period.

nodes.label: Two-Stage IRB Application Process: The IRB application process consists of a documentation submission stage followed by an on-site focused supervisory review by BSD.
nodes.norm_label: two-stage irb application process: the irb application process consists of a documentation submission stage followed by an on-site focused supervisory review by bsd.

nodes.label: Bank Readiness and Roll-Out Plan: Banks must demonstrate a state of readiness with a clear IRB roll-out plan covering material portfolios before applying for advanced approach approval.
nodes.norm_label: bank readiness and roll-out plan: banks must demonstrate a state of readiness with a clear irb roll-out plan covering material portfolios before applying for advanced approach approval.

nodes.label: Application Pack Compilation Guidance: Banks must provide concise responses in the application pack to enable BSD to scope its supervisory review of the IRB application.
nodes.norm_label: application pack compilation guidance: banks must provide concise responses in the application pack to enable bsd to scope its supervisory review of the irb application.

nodes.label: IRB Implementation Plan and Milestones: Applicants must provide an overview of the IRB implementation plan, key milestones, and internal or external expertise utilised.
nodes.norm_label: irb implementation plan and milestones: applicants must provide an overview of the irb implementation plan, key milestones, and internal or external expertise utilised.

nodes.label: Rationale for Adopting Advanced Approaches: Banks must summarise their reasons for applying for the advanced IRB approaches and the objectives they aim to achieve.
nodes.norm_label: rationale for adopting advanced approaches: banks must summarise their reasons for applying for the advanced irb approaches and the objectives they aim to achieve.

nodes.label: Group Structure and Scope of Application: Banks must detail group and legal entity structure and map the scope of the IRB application to relevant asset classes on form BA 200.
nodes.norm_label: group structure and scope of application: banks must detail group and legal entity structure and map the scope of the irb application to relevant asset classes on form ba 200.

nodes.label: Permanent Exemption Portfolios: Banks must detail any portfolios for which they seek permanent exemption from the advanced approaches.
nodes.norm_label: permanent exemption portfolios: banks must detail any portfolios for which they seek permanent exemption from the advanced approaches.

nodes.label: Corporate Governance and IRB Oversight: Banks must describe the governance framework for IRB implementation, including model development, maintenance, and independent validation.
nodes.norm_label: corporate governance and irb oversight: banks must describe the governance framework for irb implementation, including model development, maintenance, and independent validation.

nodes.label: Board-Approved Credit Policy: Banks must submit a copy of the board-approved credit policy and describe any planned future changes.
nodes.norm_label: board-approved credit policy: banks must submit a copy of the board-approved credit policy and describe any planned future changes.

nodes.label: Model Validation, Development and Monitoring Policies: Banks must submit board-approved policies covering model validation, development, and monitoring.
nodes.norm_label: model validation, development and monitoring policies: banks must submit board-approved policies covering model validation, development, and monitoring.

nodes.label: IRB Self-Assessment Schedules: Banks must complete and submit schedules 1, 2 and 3 of the IRB self-assessment templates published by the SARB.
nodes.norm_label: irb self-assessment schedules: banks must complete and submit schedules 1, 2 and 3 of the irb self-assessment templates published by the sarb.

nodes.label: Rating and Risk Estimation System Documentation: Banks must complete Annexure B for each model to be used under the IRB approach, including all relevant supporting documentation.
nodes.norm_label: rating and risk estimation system documentation: banks must complete annexure b for each model to be used under the irb approach, including all relevant supporting documentation.

nodes.label: Credit Risk Rating System Register: Banks must complete and submit a Credit Risk Rating System Register as specified by the SARB.
nodes.norm_label: credit risk rating system register: banks must complete and submit a credit risk rating system register as specified by the sarb.

nodes.label: South African Environment Model Tailoring: Banks must describe the process followed to tailor models to the South African environment and branch management's input into model development.
nodes.norm_label: south african environment model tailoring: banks must describe the process followed to tailor models to the south african environment and branch management's input into model development.

nodes.label: Rating System Experience Requirement: Banks must demonstrate they meet the experience requirement by detailing how long their rating and scoring systems have been in operation.
nodes.norm_label: rating system experience requirement: banks must demonstrate they meet the experience requirement by detailing how long their rating and scoring systems have been in operation.

nodes.label: Use Test Compliance: Banks must summarise compliance with the use test, showing how rating systems are integral to credit approval, risk reporting, and internal capital allocation.
nodes.norm_label: use test compliance: banks must summarise compliance with the use test, showing how rating systems are integral to credit approval, risk reporting, and internal capital allocation.

nodes.label: Regulatory vs Internal Parameter Estimates: Banks must outline any differences between parameter estimates used for regulatory capital purposes and those used internally.
nodes.norm_label: regulatory vs internal parameter estimates: banks must outline any differences between parameter estimates used for regulatory capital purposes and those used internally.

nodes.label: Credit Risk Stress Testing Approach: Banks must describe their credit risk stress testing approach and demonstrate compliance with regulation 23(11)(b)(ix).
nodes.norm_label: credit risk stress testing approach: banks must describe their credit risk stress testing approach and demonstrate compliance with regulation 23(11)(b)(ix).

nodes.label: Data Management and Technological Environment: Banks must describe their data management approach, including systems used for storing rating and parameter information, with reference to regulation 23(11)(b)(viii).
nodes.norm_label: data management and technological environment: banks must describe their data management approach, including systems used for storing rating and parameter information, with reference to regulation 23(11)(b)(viii).

nodes.label: Calibration Databases and Regulatory Reporting: Banks must describe how calibration databases and regulatory capital figures are obtained and confirm ability to submit risk-based returns within prescribed periods.
nodes.norm_label: calibration databases and regulatory reporting: banks must describe how calibration databases and regulatory capital figures are obtained and confirm ability to submit risk-based returns within prescribed periods.

nodes.label: Independent Validation Approach: Banks must describe their validation approach covering back-testing, performance monitoring, and benchmarking of rating system parameter estimates.
nodes.norm_label: independent validation approach: banks must describe their validation approach covering back-testing, performance monitoring, and benchmarking of rating system parameter estimates.

nodes.label: Validation Unit Staffing: Banks must detail the staffing of their validation unit, including approved vacancies and required skillsets.
nodes.norm_label: validation unit staffing: banks must detail the staffing of their validation unit, including approved vacancies and required skillsets.

nodes.label: Annexure B — Rating System Detail Template: Annexure B requires banks to provide structured details for each rating system including methodology, weaknesses, portfolio coverage, and approval committee information.
nodes.norm_label: annexure b — rating system detail template: annexure b requires banks to provide structured details for each rating system including methodology, weaknesses, portfolio coverage, and approval committee information.

nodes.label: Parameter Estimates and Capital Information Table: Banks must complete a table providing exposure, EAD, PD, and LGD data as at a specified date for each rating system submitted in Annexure B.
nodes.norm_label: parameter estimates and capital information table: banks must complete a table providing exposure, ead, pd, and lgd data as at a specified date for each rating system submitted in annexure b.

nodes.norm_label: gn 5/2014 (outsourcing) — applicability of this guidance note: guidance applies to outsourcing of material business activities and functions defined by potential impact on operations or risk management capability if disrupted.

nodes.author: Prudential Authority
nodes.norm_label: banks act guidance note 3/2025 — climate-related disclosures for banks

nodes.label: GN 3/2025 (Climate Disclosures) — Introduction: Climate-related risks pose direct threats to bank safety, soundness, and financial system stability, requiring proactive identification and disclosure.
nodes.norm_label: gn 3/2025 (climate disclosures) — introduction: climate-related risks pose direct threats to bank safety, soundness, and financial system stability, requiring proactive identification and disclosure.

nodes.label: GN 3/2025 (Climate Disclosures) — Principles and conceptual foundations for disclosures: Establishes foundational principles for consistent, comparable climate risk disclosure methodologies across banks.
nodes.norm_label: gn 3/2025 (climate disclosures) — principles and conceptual foundations for disclosures: establishes foundational principles for consistent, comparable climate risk disclosure methodologies across banks.

nodes.label: GN 3/2025 (Climate Disclosures) — Supervisory expectations: Banks must produce high-quality, decision-useful climate-related disclosure reports satisfying supervisory principles.
nodes.norm_label: gn 3/2025 (climate disclosures) — supervisory expectations: banks must produce high-quality, decision-useful climate-related disclosure reports satisfying supervisory principles.

nodes.label: GN 3/2025 (Climate Disclosures) — Governance: Banks must disclose governance structures, oversight mechanisms, and board-level controls for climate-related risks.
nodes.norm_label: gn 3/2025 (climate disclosures) — governance: banks must disclose governance structures, oversight mechanisms, and board-level controls for climate-related risks.

nodes.label: GN 3/2025 (Climate Disclosures) — Strategy: Banks must disclose how material climate risks affect business model, strategy, and financial performance.
nodes.norm_label: gn 3/2025 (climate disclosures) — strategy: banks must disclose how material climate risks affect business model, strategy, and financial performance.

nodes.label: GN 3/2025 (Climate Disclosures) — Risk management: Banks must describe processes for identifying, assessing, and monitoring climate-related risks and strategy resilience.

nodes.label: GN 3/2025 (Climate Disclosures) — Concentration risk: Banks must disclose concentration exposure effects to counterparties facing material transition or physical climate risks.

nodes.label: GN 6/2022 (Business Risk) — Introduction: Banks must conduct evidence-based risk assessments to understand vulnerability to money laundering, terrorist financing, and proliferation financing.
nodes.norm_label: gn 6/2022 (business risk) — introduction: banks must conduct evidence-based risk assessments to understand vulnerability to money laundering, terrorist financing, and proliferation financing.

nodes.label: GN 6/2022 (Business Risk) — Identification of ML/TF/PF risk: Banks must identify ML/TF/PF risks by considering national risk assessments, legal frameworks, and prescribed significant risk areas.
nodes.norm_label: gn 6/2022 (business risk) — identification of ml/tf/pf risk: banks must identify ml/tf/pf risks by considering national risk assessments, legal frameworks, and prescribed significant risk areas.

nodes.label: GN 6/2022 (Business Risk) — Assessing ML/TF/PF risk: Banks must determine likelihood and impact of identified ML/TF/PF threats on the institution, sector, and national economy.
nodes.norm_label: gn 6/2022 (business risk) — assessing ml/tf/pf risk: banks must determine likelihood and impact of identified ml/tf/pf threats on the institution, sector, and national economy.

nodes.label: GN 6/2022 (Business Risk) — Trigger Events: Banks must review risk assessments and AML/CFT controls when trigger events occur.
nodes.norm_label: gn 6/2022 (business risk) — trigger events: banks must review risk assessments and aml/cft controls when trigger events occur.

nodes.label: GN 6/2022 (Business Risk) — Risk factor consideration examples: Guidance provides examples of risk factors for consideration in business risk assessments.

nodes.label: GN 6/2022 (Business Risk) — References: Document cites reference sources consulted during drafting.
nodes.norm_label: gn 6/2022 (business risk) — references: document cites reference sources consulted during drafting.

nodes.label: GN 6/2022 (Business Risk) — Terminology: Defines key terms including foreign prominent public officials and domestic prominent influential persons per the FIC Act.
nodes.norm_label: gn 6/2022 (business risk) — terminology: defines key terms including foreign prominent public officials and domestic prominent influential persons per the fic act.

nodes.author: Prudential Authority

nodes.label: GN 9/2022 (IRB Credit Models) — Introduction: Contextual introduction explaining the PA's discussion paper and guidance scope.
nodes.norm_label: gn 9/2022 (irb credit models) — introduction: contextual introduction explaining the pa's discussion paper and guidance scope.

nodes.label: GN 9/2022 (IRB Credit Models) — Model documentation quality: IRB banks must prepare high-quality model development and validation documentation for PA review.
nodes.norm_label: gn 9/2022 (irb credit models) — model documentation quality: irb banks must prepare high-quality model development and validation documentation for pa review.

nodes.label: GN 9/2022 (IRB Credit Models) — LGD estimates for defaulted loans: IRB banks must estimate LGDs for defaulted loans to capture unexpected recovery losses.
nodes.norm_label: gn 9/2022 (irb credit models) — lgd estimates for defaulted loans: irb banks must estimate lgds for defaulted loans to capture unexpected recovery losses.

nodes.label: GN 9/2022 (IRB Credit Models) — Quality and representativeness of development datasets: Banks developing credit risk models for low-default portfolios must ensure data quality and may use external data and expert judgment.
nodes.norm_label: gn 9/2022 (irb credit models) — quality and representativeness of development datasets: banks developing credit risk models for low-default portfolios must ensure data quality and may use external data and expert judgment.

nodes.label: GN 9/2022 (IRB Credit Models) — The definition and incorporation of downturn in LGDs and EADs: IRB banks must incorporate economic downturn conditions in LGD and EAD estimates.
nodes.norm_label: gn 9/2022 (irb credit models) — the definition and incorporation of downturn in lgds and eads: irb banks must incorporate economic downturn conditions in lgd and ead estimates.
